question: Does Pippa degrade terminal Pi responsiveness or correctness?

sourceFindings.finding: The first text chunk is displayed immediately; subsequent chunks are batched for 80 ms. This does not explain multi-second model latency by itself.
Pippa replaces the base coding prompt, selects its own extensions and skills, and uses separate per-conversation sessions.
Pippa discourages progress preambles; progress-like text is not equivalent to a completed answer.
Memory and recent conversation handover may add context; idle summarization starts after 20 seconds above 60% context use. These features were not active in the fresh-session fixture comparison.

A loop brake stops repeated failed or identical calls and caps calls per answer. Terminal baseline has no such brake. In the Saluki-off terminal ledger test, the model read the same successful result 39 times before the 180-second timeout.

Pippa disables repository AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md context and uses its own working directory and bundled skills. A normal terminal session can have relevant project instructions that are absent in Pippa. The controlled fixture runs disable project context in every arm.

experiment.engine: Same installed Saluki server on port 65070
experiment.sampling: Identical installed server defaults; not optimized for off

profiles.pippa: Pippa base prompt and all 23 tools
profiles.stock: Stock Pi base prompt, same Pippa extensions, skills, and all 23 tools
profiles.lean-stock: Stock Pi base prompt, same extensions/skills, only five relevant tools exposed

experiment.order: Pippa/stock/lean in repeat 1; lean/stock/Pippa in repeat 2, per task
experiment.scope: Prompt/tool ablation over RPC, not a timing comparison of the macOS GUI against the terminal renderer. Stock arm retains Pippa helpers and is not an unmodified terminal session.
limits: Two tasks with two repeats are diagnostic only, not a general quality benchmark.
No clean-cache reset between requests; live desktop background load persists.
Native/document/web responses use deterministic fixtures; no personal app writes.
This isolates base prompt and advertised tools, not memory, conversation history, application startup, or rendering.

conclusion: Current startup defaults differ: K2 low in terminal versus Saluki medium in Pippa. They cannot establish an application-layer speed difference.
The 12-run ablation does not show a general quality regression from Pippa base prompt. Both full-tool prompt variants remain fallible.
Reducing advertised tools reduces prompt tokens and practical latency in these tasks, but does not improve factual reliability. No production tool pruning was applied.
Pippa rendering introduces an 80 ms update batch after immediate first text. No evidence here attributes multi-second response delay to that rendering path.
Long-session memory/compaction, GUI cold-start latency and real native-app tool duration remain outside this fresh-session fixture experiment.
